executive_summary: Comprehensive evidence-grounded strategy to grow Acme Textiles from ₹1.8 Cr baseline revenue to ₹3 Cr target revenue without increasing raw yarn supplier concentration.
current_situation: Acme Textiles (Tirupur, Tamil Nadu) operates with 12 employees and ₹1.8 Cr annual revenue. The business has a 68/100 readiness score, but displays high supplier concentration risk with >60% of raw cotton yarn sourced from a single supplier.

key_findings.title: High Raw Material Supplier Concentration
key_findings.description: Over 60% of cotton yarn raw material is sourced from a single regional vendor, creating supply chain vulnerability.

key_findings.title: Significant Revenue Target Gap
key_findings.description: Reaching ₹3 Cr target revenue requires ₹1.2 Cr incremental growth (66% revenue expansion).

key_findings.title: Strong Export & Financial Readiness Foundation
key_findings.description: Financial Readiness (70/100) and Export Readiness (65/100) indicate capacity to expand B2B sales in UAE and Singapore.

recommendations.title: Diversify Raw Yarn Suppliers in Tamil Nadu & Gujarat
rationales: Onboard 2 additional verified yarn mills to reduce primary vendor concentration below 40%.

recommendations.title: Launch B2B E-Commerce Catalog for Direct Buyers
rationales: Direct B2B portal expands buyer base without increasing raw supplier dependence.

action_items: Audit existing yarn contracts and request quotes from 3 alternative spinners in Surat & Coimbatore.
Upload fabric & yarn product specs (OEKO-TEX certified) to digital B2B catalog.
Initiate direct B2B buyer sampling for UAE textile importers.
Place initial trial order with secondary yarn supplier to establish backup credit terms.

assumptions: Stable raw cotton yarn pricing across South India textile hubs.
Export demand in UAE and Singapore remains consistent.
limitations: Requires working capital allocation for initial trial yarn batches.
